Class Toggleable

public abstract class Toggleable extends SettingHolder implements Listenable
A named, describable thing that can be switched on and off and owns settings.

Shared by Module and by HUD elements. The old client had this class too, but both subclasses redeclared name, description and their accessors anyway, and Module kept a second settings list that shadowed the inherited one so only one of the two was ever saved. Here the state lives in exactly one place.

Implementing Listenable is what lets an instance stay subscribed to the event bus permanently while its handlers go quiet when it is off.

Instances are always constructed disabled. A subclass that is enabled by default is switched on by its registry once everything is up, so the onEnable() hook never runs against a half-built client.

      protected Toggleable(String name, String description)

      public final void setEnabled(boolean shouldEnable)
      Switches state and fires the matching lifecycle hook.

      Setting the state it already holds does nothing, so a config load that re-asserts the current value will not run onEnable() twice.
